items.title: Melaka polls: Pas, Umno must close old wounds and strengthen ties
items.summary: MELAKA: Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said party members and their Umno counterparts should put aside their past political differences and focus on strengthening cooperation ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16). Acknowledging that the two parties had been bitter political rivals for decades, he said past disagreements should not be allowed to undermine their renewed cooperation under the Perikatan Nasional-Barisan Nasional alliance. Tuan Ibrahim said both parties should learn from their past disagreements and move forward to strengthen their political cooperation.

items.title: Hong Kong court sentences activist Joshua Wong to 10 years on national security charge
items.summary: HONG KONG: Activist Joshua Wong, 30, who became the international face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, was sentenced on Thursday to 10 years in jail on a charge of collusion with foreign entities under the city's national security law. Wong was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and others in 2020 to request that foreign countries, institutions, organisations or individuals outside China impose sanctions or blockades, or engage in other hostile activities directed against the governments of Hong Kong and China. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Minimum wage, targeted assistance part of broader economic balancing act: Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's minimum wage policy cannot be viewed in isolation but should be seen as complementing the targeted assistance, subsidy rationalisation and affordable healthcare measures to ensure workers' income gains translate into improved household well-being, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said the government is ultimately working towards two key objectives, namely building a sustainable economy and preserving social cohesion. he said.

items.title: Malacca Securities Sees 63.6pct upside for Impact Capital, sets 36 sen fair value
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malacca Securities has assigned a fair value of 36 sen per share to Impact Capital Holdings Bhd, representing a potential upside of 63.6 per cent from its initial public offering (IPO) price of 22 sen. It said Impact Capital was well-positioned to benefit from Sarawak's ongoing digital infrastructure development, supported by its established presence in the state's information and communications technology (ICT) sector. Malacca Securities said ICT integration contributed 72.7 per cent of the group's FY26 revenue, while Sarawak accounted for 75.1 per cent.

items.title: Negri Sembilan Education Department probes viral video of 'zombie-like' student
items.summary: NILAI: The Negri Sembilan Education Department is investigating a viral video showing a student in a zombie-like state at a secondary school in the district. The video, which went viral on Threads, carried claims that the student, purportedly a Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidate, was under the influence of a substance known as "piu piu". The incident has also raised questions about how the substance, if drugs were indeed involved, could have been brought into the school.

items.title: IOI Corp's solar power venture to unlock land bank potential
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Corp Bhd's venture into large-scale solar energy with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) is expected to unlock value from its land assets while providing a new source of recurring income, says CIMB Securities. "We estimate the project could generate annual net profit of RM50 to RM60 million. CIMB Securities estimated that the project could generate a combined annual net profit contribution and lease rental income of RM22 million to RM24.5 million from 2029.

items.title: Anwar: Differences of opinion between ministries do not mean government is divided
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Differences in views or approaches between ministries do not reflect divisions within the government, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said the government ensured proper coordination between ministries to maintain policy consistency, avoid overlapping functions and ensure decisions were guided by public interest, national development priorities and the government's financial capacity. Anwar said that, to ensure effective governance, all government policies and decisions must undergo the necessary deliberation and coordination.

items.title: Tun Faisal: Bersatu stayed away from PN seat talks over legal implications
items.summary: MELAKA: Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) did not attend Perikatan Nasional's (PN) seat talks because participating would carry severe legal implications and validate constitutional violations committed by Pas, the party said. Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said the party's absence from the meeting, which Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man raised, was an intentional, principled decision officially communicated by Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali. When contacted, Tun Faisal said attending would create a misleading impression that Pas had committed no wrongdoing, effectively endorsing decisions made in breach of the coalition's constitution.

items.title: Malaysian shoppers turn selective as Asean growth fails to lift FMCG spending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cautious household spending and increasingly selective shoppers are making it harder for fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies in Malaysia and other Asean countries to capture growth. "Growth in Southeast Asia is not disappearing - it is becoming harder to capture," said Praneeth Yendamuri, partner and head of Asia Pacific Consumer Products practice at Bain. "Consumer products companies can no longer rely on broad-based consumption growth or traditional definitions of premium and value."

items.title: Motorists to enjoy 50pct toll discount for two days in conjunction with Deepavali
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists will enjoy a 50 per cent toll discount for two days in conjunction with Deepavali, with the government allocating RM20.11 million in compensation to participating highway concessionaires. The initiative covers Class 1 private vehicles at all toll plazas, as well as Class 2 vehicles at the Penang Bridge. However, the discount will not apply at border toll plazas, namely the Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) toll plaza on the North-South Expressway and Tanjung Kupang toll plaza on the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link.

items.title: AirAsia, Capital A shares surge as oil prices plunge
items.summary: As at 9.30am, AirAsia Group's shares had climbed as much as 20.88 per cent, or 9.5 sen, to 55 sen from Wednesday's close of 45.5 sen. The stock subsequently eased to 52 sen, still up 14.29 per cent, or 6.5 sen, with more than 26 million shares changing hands. Meanwhile, its associate Capital A rose as much as 15.22 per cent, or 3.5 sen, to 26.5 sen from Wednesday's close of 23 sen. At the time of writing, Capital A was trading at 25.5 sen, up 10.87 per cent, or 2.5 sen, with more than 21 million shares traded.

items.title: Singapore shoppers make a beeline for Johor's Little India bazaar
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The annual Deepavali bazaar in Johor Baru's Little India has drawn local shoppers and visitors from Singapore seeking traditional snacks, clothing and other festive goods. The annual bazaar offers a wide selection of goods, including traditional snacks, clothing, home decorations and women's accessories. Singaporean visitor T. Murthy, 78, said he and his family travelled to the city every year to buy traditional snacks sold at the bazaar.

items.title: Rapid KL train congestion: Anthony Loke vows fix after PM’s directive
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 5 — The Transport Ministry is actively working to resolve train service congestion and overcome technical challenges faced by rail operators, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. We will resolve these technical issues to improve the service,” he said. On Oct 30, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim directed the Transport Minister to swiftly resolve train congestion issues, expressing concern that they disrupt the public’s daily routine.

items.title: Citi employee killed in shooting at Florida office, suspect dead
items.summary: NEW YORK: A Citigroup employee was killed in a shooting at the bank's office in Tampa, Florida on Wednesday, Chief Executive Jane Fraser said, while authorities said the suspect involved was also dead. In a memo to staff, Fraser said the bank was still learning the details of what happened and was working closely with local law enforcement. Hilsboro County Sheriff Chad Chronister said in a statement earlier on Wednesday that "the suspect involved in the Citibank Active Threat scene is deceased."

items.title: Anwar heads to Melaka to drum up Pakatan momentum ahead of Nov 14 polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to attend five programmes in Melaka tomorrow, including participating in Pakatan Harapan (PH) campaign activities in conjunction with the Melaka State Election. Anwar said two of the programmes he would be attending are the 2026 Prime Minister’s Golden Hand Award (MATEPM) ceremony and the Melaka State Madani Aspirations Tour. “Insya-Allah, I will be in Melaka tomorrow for several engagements in this historic state.

items.title: Monsoon aid brings relief to 3,000 residents in Tumpat
items.summary: TUMPAT: Food and essential supplies distributed ahead of the northeast monsoon have brought relief to more than 3,000 residents in 12 villages. Teluk Renjuna villager Mohd Faiza Ibrahim, 46, said most residents tended to stay home during the monsoon as persistent rain and rising river levels made it difficult to travel. "Boats are the main mode of transport for residents.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia opens firmer on improved global sentiment
items.summary: The benchmark index opened 6.72 points higher at 1,623.28. In active trade, AirAsia rose eight sen to 53.5 sen, Capital A gained three sen to 26 sen, while Dagang Nexchange, VS Industry and MMAG were half a sen lower at 41.5 sen, 33 sen and two sen, respectively. Nestle led the top gainers, rising RM1.00 to RM94.50, while Hong Leong Bank gained 26 sen to RM21.50, Allianz rose 20 sen to RM19.72, Hong Leong Financial gained 18 sen to RM17.64, and PPB advanced 14 sen to RM9.00.

items.title: Heading east for Deepavali? Concessionaire releases travel time advisory for KLK and LPT1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Highway concessionaire AFA Prime Berhad has activated its Travel Time Advisory for the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway (KLK) and the East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) ahead of an anticipated holiday traffic surge for Deepavali. The staggered travel schedule aims to ease bottlenecks across the arterial eastern corridor, particularly at the high-volume Gombak, Bentong, and Jabor toll plazas that link the Klang Valley to Pahang, Terengganu, and Kelantan. For outbound journeys from Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Saturday, Nov 7, motorists passing through the Gombak Toll Plaza are advised to stagger their departures according to their destination.

items.title: Seven foreigners held, RM1.08m in drugs seized in Bukit Mertajam raids
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 5 — Police arrested seven foreigners and seized suspected methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA) powder and ketamine worth RM1.08 million during raids on two premises in Bukit Tengah here on Nov 1. Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT) district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said a team from the district Narcotics Crime Investigation Division raided the premises at 12.50 am following surveillance and intelligence gathering. Nik Aminuddin said urine screening tests revealed that two of the suspects tested positive for methamphetamine, while the other five tested negative.

items.title: Deepavali toll relief: 50pc discount on major highways this Friday and Saturday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Motorists travelling across the country for the Deepavali celebrations will enjoy a 50 per cent toll discount on Friday and Saturday, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi announced today. Putrajaya estimates the two-day toll concession will require approximately RM20.11 million in federal compensation payouts to highway concessionaires, subject to post-holiday traffic volume verifications. The discount applies to private Class 1 passenger vehicles across all interstate expressways, alongside Class 2 commercial vehicles crossing the Penang Bridge.

items.title: Explainer: Will Bank Negara raise OPR to 3pct? What it means for your loans
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Will Bank Negara Malaysia raise interest rates today? The central bank will announce its final interest rate decision of the year at 3pm, with most economists expecting it to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75 per cent. Some economists believe this gives Bank Negara room to "normalise" interest rates by returning the OPR to its previous level.

items.title: Two women detained after RM3.47mil agarwood seizure in Kelantan
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Two women were detained after police seized agarwood worth RM3.47 million in a raid on a house in Kampung Baharu Cherang Hangus, Chicha Tinggi. He said inspections of the house, a storeroom and an old factory next to the residence uncovered 197 agarwood logs and 310.8kg of agarwood pieces, as well as seven plastic drums and 11 documents. "The arrests and seized items were subsequently handed over to the Kelantan Forestry Department," he said.

items.title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's stunning midterm defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028. But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars such as Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful appeal has already drawn comparisons with former president Barack Obama. Republicans in turmoil The MAGA coalition that propelled Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday's midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat to discuss RON95 quality, landfill woes, foreign drivers today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The quality of RON95 petrol samples, solid waste landfill mitigation, and enforcement against foreigners driving without valid licences will take centre stage in the Dewan Rakyat today. In the same session, Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong) will ask the housing and local government minister about long-term strategies for critical open dumpsites under rural local authorities, as well as mitigation plans for districts without Waste-to-Energy plants. During the oral question-and-answer session, Dr Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) will ask the transport minister to elaborate on enforcement mechanisms against foreigners, including United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees cardholders and undocumented immigrants, driving motor vehicles without a valid licence.

items.title: Police dismiss viral claim of teen electrocuted to death on mall massage chair
items.summary: KAJANG: A viral post claiming that a teenage girl died after being electrocuted while using a massage chair at a shopping mall is false. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said investigations found no such incident had occurred. He said police received a report at 7.50pm yesterday concerning a Facebook post carrying the claim.

items.title: Penang ferry free for Malaysians on Nov 8 for Deepavali
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — The Penang Port Commission (PPC) and Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) will offer free ferry rides to Malaysian citizens on Nov 8 in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration. PPC chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the free ferry rides would be available to passengers departing from both Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH) in Butterworth and Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda (PRTU) in George Town. “The free ferry service will operate according to the latest timetable.

items.title: French blood bank hit in latest cyberattack on fridges
items.summary: PARIS: The cooling system of France's blood bank has been hit by a cyberattack similar to the hacker attack targeting refrigeration systems across Europe earlier this week, the EFS bank said on Wednesday, reported German Press Agency (dpa). Cooling rooms at three of the bank's locations have been affected, EFS said. No samples or blood products were compromised, according to EFS.

items.title: It is not a split, it is ‘policy deliberation’: Anwar cools talk of ministry feud over budgets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said differences of views between ministries do not necessarily reflect a split in the government but are part of policy deliberation, with matters needing a collective decision go to the Cabinet. The PM said the government ensures orderly coordination between ministries to keep policy consistent and avoid overlapping functions. On who decides the official position, Anwar said every government policy and decision must go through proper deliberation and coordination.

items.title: Texas data centres face uncertain future after Hinojosa wins governor's race
items.summary: Big Tech companies including Meta, Google and Microsoft have announced major data center projects in the state over the past two years. The data center industry there had already come under pressure before the midterms. By the time Texas halted data centers connecting to its grid, state grid operator ERCOT said it was tracking more than 400 gigawatts of data center projects – roughly equivalent to what it would take to power the entire US South – seeking to connect to the grid.

items.title: Boy, 6, drowned while fishing alone in Kulai pond, police rule out foul play
items.summary: KULAI: Police have ruled out foul play in the drowning of a 6-year-old boy found in a retention pond near Taman Sungai Mas yesterday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said initial investigations revealed the boy's parents left for work at 6.30am, leaving him asleep with his 17-year-old sister. Tan said investigations showed the victim was believed to have gone to the pond alone to fish, following the discovery of a fishing rod near the scene.

items.title: Dodol sales double amid Melaka election campaign
items.summary: MELAKA: Sales of traditional Melaka dodol have doubled for a local producer, driven by an influx of political party campaign teams and visitors from outside the state during the 16th Melaka election campaign. Nur Aliyah Zaidi, 28, whose family has been making dodol for four generations, said the presence of campaign teams and visitors from outside the state had contributed to an increase in customers visiting their premises. Nur Aliyah said visits by political party campaign teams usually increased towards the end of the campaign period, based on her family's experience in previous elections.

items.title: Dr Solehin says brother Dr Akmal opens doors on Bemban campaign trail
items.summary: JASIN: Bersama's Bemban candidate Dr Solehin Saleh said his younger brother, Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, had helped him engage rural Malay voters. Dr Solehin said being Dr Akmal's elder brother had opened doors during the campaign, particularly when meeting rural and elderly Malay voters. "People naturally recognise the family connection and say, 'Oh, you are Dr Akmal's brother'.

items.title: Carlsberg Malaysia says it was never a sponsor of Hyrox Kuala Lumpur, cites local laws and cultural sensitivities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Carlsberg Malaysia has clarified that it was never a sponsor of Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 and holds no commercial involvement in the upcoming fitness competition, further defusing a controversy over marketing graphics that had drawn permit threats from the Youth and Sports Ministry. In a statement posted to Instagram yesterday, the brewer explained that a newly unveiled regional partnership between Hyrox and Carlsberg in Asia applies exclusively to events staged in Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Vietnam, leaving Malaysia deliberately omitted from the arrangement. The multi-day indoor fitness race is slated to take place from Dec 10 to 13 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) in Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Govt mulls three missile systems after Norway’s NSM permit cancellation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The Ministry of Defence is in the final stages of evaluating three options for a surface-to-surface missile (SSM) system after the Norwegian government cancelled the export permit for the Naval Strike Missile (NSM). The ministry said the selection of the system would take into account operational requirements, integration compatibility with naval vessels, costs and the procurement timeline. As for the first LCS, KD Maharaja Lela, the vessel is currently undergoing Harbour Acceptance Trials after completing several shipyard acceptance tests.

items.title: Gold rises after biggest daily gain since August, with US payrolls in focus
items.summary: FUNDAMENTALS Spot gold was up 0.6 per cent at US$4,082.76 per ounce by 0036 GMT, after climbing about 3.4 per cent on Monday. US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.5 per cent to US$4,092.90. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.3 per cent to US$52.37 per ounce, platinum gained 0.6 per cent to US$1,505.85 and palladium dropped 0.1 per cent to US$1,003.83.

items.title: Melaka polls: Evaluate Ab Rauf's leadership based on facts, not baseless claims
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Melaka voters should focus on the state government's achievements rather than be influenced by baseless claims when deciding whom to support in the Nov 14 state election. Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Johan Abd Aziz said caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh's administrative track record spoke for itself and should be the basis for voters to evaluate the state government. Also present was Ab Rauf, who is Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman.

items.title: AI push to transform government, unlock growth for Malaysian businesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Amazon Web Services (AWS) said Malaysian software companies using its cloud platform to develop and deploy solutions recorded an average 30 per cent increase in cloud and artificial intelligence (AI) workloads between 2024 and 2025. The growth indicates that local technology firms are handling larger computing workloads as they develop new digital products, enhance existing applications and integrate AI capabilities into solutions for businesses across various industries. In a statement, AWS Malaysia country manager Hussein Mohd Ali said the nationwide Semarak AI Malaysia initiative was designed to accelerate the country's transition from being primarily a consumer of AI technology to becoming a developer and exporter of AI solutions, talent and intellectual property.

items.title: Focus Point expands premium eyewear portfolio
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Focus Point Vision Care Group Sdn Bhd, Malaysia's largest optical retail chain, is strengthening its foothold in the premium eyewear market as part of its continued efforts to broaden its retail offerings and cater to the evolving preferences of discerning consumers. The company, a subsidiary of Main Market-listed Focus Point Holdings Bhd, and which has a nationwide network of more than 210 outlets, has established a strong presence in Malaysia's optical retail industry. The opening ceremony was attended by Johor Bahru Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Datuk Jeffrey Lai Jiun Jye, Focus Point Holdings Bhd president and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Liaw Choon Liang, and IGB REIT Management Sdn Bhd deputy CEO of retail Rennie Lee.

items.title: Melaka polls: Bersatu skipped PN seat talks before fielding candidates, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: MELAKA: Bersatu did not attend Perikatan Nasional's seat allocation negotiations before fielding candidates against the coalition in the Melaka election, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said. The party later decided to field candidates against PN, despite maintaining that it remained part of the coalition. Tuan Ibrahim also questioned Bersatu's commitment to the coalition, citing its complaint to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) seeking PN's deregistration.

items.title: KLIA altercation: Special Branch duo sue MCBA chief Shuhaily for assault, defamation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Two Special Branch policemen have filed a civil lawsuit against Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, suing him in his personal capacity for alleged assault, battery, false imprisonment, and defamation following an altercation at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). Shuhaily pleaded not guilty to both charges and remains out on court bail. The plaintiffs alleged that upon discovering they were Special Branch personnel, Shuhaily grew incensed, questioned why police intelligence was monitoring MCBA personnel, and initiated a physical confrontation.

items.title: Zahid: 2026 Cyber Crime Bill allows courts to freeze scam proceeds before suspects are charged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The 2026 Cyber Crime Bill provides powers for the court to issue property restriction orders to prevent scam proceeds from being dissipated, even before a suspect has been charged. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the provision under clause 54 enables the court to issue orders to prevent or stop violations of the law, thereby protecting victims of cybercrime. “Among the orders that can be issued include cessation orders, restitution orders to victims, compliance orders, and property restriction orders to prevent assets such as scam proceeds from being dissipated,” he said in a written Dewan Rakyat reply yesterday.

items.title: Fadillah says Melaka visit strictly for official business, not linked to state political developments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof has clarified that his presence in Melaka today was strictly on official business and has no connection to the state’s political developments. Fadillah, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister, said his visit was to officiate the 2026 CGNEI Gas Turbine Power Generation Committee Annual Conference at the EPH Training Centre, Edra Melaka Power Plant, in Kuala Sungai Baru. He noted that the conference, also attended by Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, is an initiative by CGN Energy International (CGNEI) and Edra Power Holdings Sdn Bhd through the establishment of the CGNEI Gas Turbine Skills Training Centre (CGNEI GTSTC) in Melaka.

items.title: Anwar: Hospital Seberang Jaya’s new cardiac services to cut waiting times, ease pressure on Penang Hospital
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 5 — Hospital Seberang Jaya (HSJ) has made history as the first Level 2 hospital in Peninsular Malaysia to offer angiogram and angioplasty procedures, expanding access to specialised cardiac care for residents of Seberang Perai and surrounding areas. Congratulating the hospital’s staff, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the expansion of services is expected to shorten waiting times and reduce the need for patients to seek treatment at Penang Hospital (HPP). Meanwhile, Penang State Cardiology Services head Datuk Dr Mohamed Jahangir Abdul Wahab said the operation of HSJ’s Invasive Cardiology Laboratory, which enables coronary angiogram and angioplasty procedures, reflects the government’s commitment to widening access to quality healthcare.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: RON95 quality, haze preparedness and maritime surveillance among key issues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — The quality of RON95 petrol samples, mitigation of solid waste landfills, and enforcement against foreigners driving without valid licences are among the key issues slated for discussion in the Dewan Rakyat today. Siti Mastura Muhammad (PN-Kepala Batas) is scheduled to ask the Transport Minister to elaborate on enforcement mechanisms against foreigners, including United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders and undocumented immigrants driving motor vehicles without a valid licence, during the oral question-and-answer session. The committee stage debate and winding-up session for Budget 2027 is scheduled to run until Nov 26, according to the Dewan Rakyat calendar.

items.title: Learn from Trump’s midterm defeat: Guan Eng warns Putrajaya over ‘phantom growth’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — DAP’s Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the federal government to heed the political reckoning of the US midterm elections, warning that strong headline economic numbers will not save Putrajaya from voter backlash if everyday citizens continue to grapple with escalating living costs. Lim noted that despite the US registering 3.4 per cent gross domestic product growth in the third quarter of 2026, voters remained unswayed because gains were concentrated in isolated sectors, creating a bifurcated two-tier economy that left ordinary households behind. “These challenges are compounded by the government’s hike in compliance costs and taxes last year,” Lim said.

items.title: Budget 2027: Can monthly EPF withdrawals keep retirees from running out of money?
items.summary: The government is encouraging Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members to consider taking their savings through monthly withdrawals instead of withdrawing the entire amount at once, with the aim of helping them manage their finances and preserve their retirement income for longer. Under Budget 2027, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that EPF members aged 55 and 60 could opt for monthly withdrawals under the i-Emas scheme, allowing savings retained with the fund to continue earning annual dividends. He said monthly withdrawals could help reduce the risk of retirees exhausting their savings too quickly by encouraging more disciplined spending while allowing the unwithdrawn balance to continue earning dividends.

items.title: Brickfields Deepavali traders turn to TikTok as shoppers shun relocated bazaar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — After weeks of sluggish sales, Deepavali bazaar traders in Brickfields are making a final push on TikTok to drive last-minute sales ahead of the festival on Sunday. Gunaseelan Subramaniam, a clothing vendor who has traded at the Brickfields Deepavali bazaar for 25 years, said his old spot drew a stronger crowd during breakfast and lunch hours on working days. Gunaseelan Subramaniam, a clothing vendor at the Deepavali bazaar in Brickfields said he hardly made RM1,000 during his last weekend sale.

items.title: Fadhlina warns of ‘scrolling generation’ as gadgets erode reading habits among youth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The emergence of digital gadgets has increasingly undermined reading habits among younger generations, giving rise to a “scrolling generation”, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said reading should be part of everyday life, rather than merely a leisure activity, to nurture a more knowledgeable generation. Fadhlina said encouraging a reading culture among Malaysians, particularly students at schools and universities, was a key government priority, adding that the ministry introduced the ‘Jom Baca Bersama 10 Minit’ programme to promote reading among pre-school, primary and secondary school pupils.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Price of RON97 down by 20 sen, RON95 and diesel drop by 15 sen respectively tomorrow
items.summary: Meanwhile, the price of subsidised RON95 through Budi95 remains at RM1.99 per liter, with the government bearing a subsidy of RM2.28 per liter, or 53 percent of the unsubsidised price for the period. For Budi Diesel, the price for eligible recipients remains at RM2.10 per liter, involving a government subsidy of RM3.02 per liter, or 59 percent of the unsubsidised price. Additionally, the price of petrol under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) remains at RM2.05 per liter, while diesel under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) remains at RM2.15 per liter.

items.title: Penang e-hailing drivers to get one-off RM600 aid from 2027
items.summary: State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the application criteria for the Special E-Hailing Incentive Assistance would be announced next month. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, when tabling the 2027 State Budget on Friday (Oct 30), announced that the state government would introduce a one-off Special E-Hailing Incentive Assistance of RM600 for eligible drivers, with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million. The State Legislative Assembly sitting will resume tomorrow.

items.title: Mutiara Line LRT link to Penang Sentral to begin construction in 2027, completion targeted for 2031
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Construction of the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) alignment linking Macallum on the island to Penang Sentral in Seberang Perai, including a marine bridge across the Penang Strait, is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027. Preliminary works will be carried out first, followed by major construction activities, including the construction of a bridge across the Penang Strait. Zairil said the finalised Macallum-Penang Sentral alignment would feature a 5.5-kilometre (km) marine bridge across the Penang Strait, with two main stations at Macallum and Penang Sentral.

items.title: In Johor, six-year-old boy drowns after falling into reservoir while fishing
items.summary: KULAI, Nov 4 — A six-year-old boy drowned after falling into a reservoir while fishing at Jalan Budiman in Kampung Melayu Kulai here today. Kulai Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Awang Adzwan Awang Sahari said authorities received a distress call on the incident at 10.17am. Awang Adzwan said the team located the victim and carried out a rescue operation.

items.title: Over five million Malaysians to receive RM1.1b STR aid from today, says Anwar
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the disbursement is being made in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration and covers recipients from various ethnic backgrounds. Also present were Minister of Communications Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, and Minister of Digital Gobind Singh Deo. RM6 billion.

items.title: Selangor gears up for north-east monsoon, deploys 7,677 personnel for disaster response
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 4 — The Selangor state government has mobilised 7,677 personnel from various state agencies to prepare for disasters during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to continue until March 2027. State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the mobilisation involved the State Disaster Management Unit (UPBN), local authorities, district offices and relevant agencies to coordinate operations and monitor high-risk areas. Jamaliah said JPS was monitoring flood risks through 221 rainfall telemetry stations, 124 water-level monitoring stations, 140 warning sirens and 72 IP cameras.

items.title: Klang Valley raids uncover suspected luxury liquor tax-stamp scam, RM702,566 haul seized
items.summary: He said initial inspections at the warehouse found that some luxury liquor bottles allegedly bore tax stamps or customs labels with lower duty rates than those applicable to the products. However, inspections at the second premises found that all liquor bottles bore valid tax stamps, with no offences detected. The Customs Department is also investigating possible offences under Section 133(1)(c) of the Customs Act 1967.

items.title: Three boat operators among 38 Indonesians held in Selangor migrant smuggling crackdown
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Three boat operators were among 38 Indonesian nationals detained by the General Operations Force (GOF) in an operation to curb migrant smuggling along the coastal area of Kampung Sungai Gatal, near Sabak Bernam, on November 2. He said the other 35 individuals arrested comprised 24 adult men and 11 adult women. Awang Arfian said the GOF Central Brigade recorded 171 cases involving migrant smuggling activities and immigration offences from January 1 to November 4 this year.

items.title: Anwar says aid for Indian community goes beyond Mitra, more initiatives in pipeline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Government assistance for the Indian community is not only channelled through the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), but also includes various initiatives in welfare, entrepreneurship, education and social development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said such assistance was also provided through various government agencies and programmes, including the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid scheme, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), entrepreneurship financing through Tekun Nasional and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, as well as allocations for the development of Tamil schools and places of worship. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.

items.title: Malaysian prosecutors unable to find Yusoff Rawther in UK to physically serve appeal notice despite Interpol help
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — The Court of Appeal was told today that the prosecution has yet to physically serve a notice of appeal on Muhammed Yusoff Rawther, a former research assistant to a politician, who is currently in the United Kingdom (UK). “The prosecution was informed last month that efforts to locate the respondent (Muhammed Yusoff) had been unsuccessful. The DPP said the prosecution was seeking another case management date to allow efforts to locate Muhammed Yusoff and serve the notice to continue.

items.title: Penang DOSH to probe cause of fatal Paya Terubong landslide, developer told to submit documents
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — The Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is conducting an investigation to determine the actual cause of the landslide at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, covering aspects such as safety, construction, and regulatory compliance. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the investigation includes gathering information and statements from the developer, contractors, and consultants involved in the development project on the slope near the site of the incident. “The Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) held discussions yesterday (Nov 3) with civil and geotechnical consulting engineers, the developer, and the contractor to investigate and understand the root cause of the incident covering aspects of safety, construction, design, and compliance with relevant regulations as well as to propose appropriate mitigation measures and site stabilization efforts.

items.title: Police arrest 35 foreigners in Penang love scam, gold investment fraud raids
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Police arrested 35 foreign nationals suspected of involvement in an online fraud syndicate specialising in love scams and gold investment schemes during raids on two residences in Bayan Lepas, near here, last Monday. Barat Daya police chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said the suspects, comprising 33 Chinese men, one Chinese woman and one Taiwanese man, were arrested in an operation conducted by the district’s Commercial Crime Investigation Division in collaboration with the Penang Contingent Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID). “Preliminary investigations revealed that the syndicate began operating last September, targeting Chinese national women aged between 18 and 46 through the Telegram application,” he said in a statement today.
